_about: One list of tour steps, used by the automated browser tour (frontend/tour/run-tour.mjs) and meant to power the in-app tour later (same titles, captions, pages and highlights). Fields: who = demo account (owner|worker|viewer); workspace = campus|farm; path = page inside the workspace; openAsset = asset to open from the Assets list; focus = element to highlight; do = harmless actions (nothing is ever saved); dwell = seconds to stay.

steps.title: One product, two modes
steps.caption: After signing in you see your workspaces: a campus (Green Management) and a farm (Agricultural Production). The data model is the same; the mode picks the vocabulary, the stages and the headline figures.

steps.title: The campus at a glance
steps.caption: Every figure comes from the server. 'Left the lifecycle' counts the tree recorded dead, which is NOT counted in any other tile. Unavailable figures explain why instead of showing a made-up number.

steps.title: Survival is computed from recorded deaths
steps.caption: Survival = alive / (alive + recorded dead) over individually tracked assets. Removed and replaced trees are management decisions and are left out; the basis text says exactly what was counted.

steps.title: Assets and their lifecycle stage
steps.caption: Every asset shows its stage. The filter switches between active assets and the ones that left the lifecycle (dead, failed, removed, replaced).

steps.title: An asset's append-only lifecycle
steps.caption: Neem #102 is in decline (health 78 to 31). The lifecycle history is append-only: nothing is edited or deleted. Workers record stage changes; the server enforces the rules.

steps.title: Corrections need a manager and a reason
steps.caption: Going back a stage, or reinstating an exited asset, is a correction. Only a manager can record one, with a written reason, and it stays visible in the history. (Nothing is saved in this tour.)

steps.title: Everything that happened to it
steps.caption: Photos, issues, tasks, observations and lifecycle changes are merged into one history, each with who and when.

steps.title: The Botanical Operations Agent
steps.caption: Rule-based suggestions with their evidence and rule version, labelled RULE or STATISTICAL. A person accepts or dismisses each one. It is not machine learning and the screen says so.

steps.title: Map
steps.caption: Assets are positioned across the campus and coloured by health. The dead Gulmohar is not drawn: its last health reading would mislead. (Map tiles need an internet connection.)

steps.title: The farm: Agricultural Production mode
steps.caption: Same product, different mode: the headline figures are Growth, Health, Yield, Harvest and Revenue. Yield and Harvest are computed from recorded data; Revenue says it needs yield and price data.

steps.title: Harvest records
steps.caption: Each picking is recorded with a quantity, unit and grade. Weights (kg, t) are added together; counts and litres never are. The Yield figure is the recorded weight of the last 12 months, not an estimate.

steps.title: Correcting a harvest
steps.caption: A manager replaces a mistaken record with a corrected one and a reason; the original stays in the history, struck through. A correction to 0 withdraws a record. (Nothing is saved in this tour.)

steps.title: Signed in as a field worker
steps.caption: A worker can record observations and stage changes, but the correction option and decisions are gone. The server enforces this too; hiding a button is only a courtesy.

steps.title: Signed in as a viewer
steps.caption: A viewer can read everything in their workspace and change nothing: no forms, no buttons that record.

steps.title: Audit log
steps.caption: Every change above was recorded with who, what, when and a request ID. The log is append-only and only managers can read it.

steps.title: Datasets: governance before machine learning
steps.caption: Dataset licences, image origin and label review are tracked, and an approval gate blocks any claim. No dataset is approved and no model exists: future AI features are shown as planned, never faked.

steps.title: Evaluation protocols
steps.caption: The protocol for judging a future disease model is written down before any training. Thresholds that need a plant pathologist are left empty on purpose, and a protocol cannot be approved without verified sign-offs.
